name: United Arab Emirates
headline: The hub that turns oil into a global platform.
summary: A federation of seven emirates created in 1971, the country used Abu Dhabi's rent to become a commercial, financial, and logistics platform. Dubai attracts capital and talent from around the world; the risk is less solvency than dependence on an open model and an unstable regional environment.

history.title: Oil in Abu Dhabi
history.text: The discovery of major fields turns a set of trading sheikhdoms into a future rentier state.

history.title: Foundation of the federation
history.text: Six emirates unite, later joined by Ras al-Khaimah. Abu Dhabi brings the oil, Dubai the trade, and the country adopts a federal constitution.

history.title: Jebel Ali and logistics
history.text: The Jebel Ali port and free zone create a re-export model. Dubai becomes a crossroads between Asia, Africa, and Europe.

history.title: DIFC and international finance
history.text: The Dubai International Financial Centre adopts English law and its own courts. International capital gets a familiar legal enclave.

history.title: Dubai's debt crisis
history.text: Dubai World asks for a standstill. Abu Dhabi helps with restructuring: federal solidarity saves the hub's reputation.

history.title: Abraham Accords
history.text: The Emirates normalize relations with Israel. The country gains a technology partner and strengthens its image as a pragmatic power.

history.title: Targeting the next 50 years
history.text: The country launches a diversification strategy: clean energy, artificial intelligence, industry, and long-term visas to attract talent.

institutions.regime: Federation of monarchies; president from Abu Dhabi
institutions.executive: Supreme Council of Rulers, president and Prime Minister
institutions.legislature: Federal National Council, partially elected and consultative
institutions.central_bank: Central Bank of the UAE, dollar peg
institutions.law: Civil law and common law in free zones; strong emirate autonomy
institutions.fact: Free zones and specialized jurisdictions attract capital without liberalizing the whole country.

allies.name: Saudi Arabia
allies.note: Strategic neighbor and GCC partner, but economic rivalry.

allies.name: Israel
allies.note: The 2020 normalization, technology and trade cooperation.

rivals.name: Iran
rivals.note: Territorial dispute over the islands and regional rivalry.

rivals.name: Qatar
rivals.note: Hub competition and the aftermath of the 2017 blockade.

dependencies.name: Hydrocarbons
dependencies.note: Abu Dhabi remains the main source of federal revenue.

dependencies.name: Foreign labor
dependencies.note: More than 80% of the population is expatriate.

dependencies.name: Global trade
dependencies.note: The re-export model depends on stable shipping routes.

gdp_growth.note: Non-oil growth is robust: tourism, finance, logistics, and real estate offset slower crude.

inflation.note: Inflation stays contained thanks to the pegged dirham and subsidy policies, though Dubai real estate can create pressure.

debt_gdp.note: Federal debt is low and sovereign assets considerable. Sustainability is not debated in the short term.

policy_rate.note: The central bank follows the Fed to defend the peg. Higher rates make mortgages and projects more expensive.

unemployment.note: Official unemployment is very low, but it does not measure the situation of low-skilled migrant workers.

reserves.note: Reserves plus Abu Dhabi's and Dubai's sovereign funds form a very large shock absorber.

rating.note: The high rating reflects wealth per capita, low debt, and solid sovereign funds.

cds.note: The market prices very low risk, close to some developed issuers.

equity_index.note: The market benefits from real estate, banks, and IPOs. Liquidity remains concentrated in a few names.

currency.name: UAE dirham
currency.note: The dollar peg (3.6725 AED/USD) offers great nominal stability, at the price of an imported monetary policy.

strengths: Advanced diversification and a very business-friendly climate.
Reserves and sovereign funds that amply cover the debt.
risks: Dependence on foreign labor and global trade.
Regional competition and exposure to Gulf tensions.
A cyclical real estate market and opaque structures.
opportunities: Islamic finance, asset management, and fintech.
A free-trade zone for re-export to Africa and Asia.

quiz.question: How many emirates make up the United Arab Emirates?
quiz.explanation: The federation is created in 1971 by six emirates; Ras al-Khaimah joins in 1972, bringing the total to seven.
